title: Nodes
description: Resources across socrat-0/1/2/3: CPU, load, memory, disks, and network. All metrics come from node-exporter.

panels.title: Ready
panels.description: Ready=false or unknown for 15 minutes, including cordoned nodes. Color represents alert state at the end of the selected period: green is normal, amber is pending. No telemetry means Kubernetes state or rule-evaluation data is unavailable. Open the node to inspect it in Rancher.

targets.expr: ((max(2 * ALERTS{alertname="KubeNodeNotReady",node="$node",alertstate="firing"} or ALERTS{alertname="KubeNodeNotReady",node="$node",alertstate="pending"})) or (0 * max(kube_node_status_condition{job="kube-state-metrics",node="$node",condition="Ready",status="true"}))) and on() ((max(up{job="kube-state-metrics"}) == 1) and on() (time() - max(timestamp(up{job="kube-state-metrics"})) < 90) and on() (time() - max(prometheus_rule_group_last_evaluation_timestamp_seconds{rule_group=~".*;socrat.nodes.health"}) < 90))

panels.title: Memory pressure
panels.description: MemoryPressure reported by Kubernetes for 5 minutes. This is not simply high RAM utilization. Color represents alert state at the end of the selected period: green is normal, amber is pending. No telemetry means Kubernetes state or rule-evaluation data is unavailable. Open the node to inspect it in Rancher.

targets.expr: ((max(2 * ALERTS{alertname="KubeNodePressure",node="$node",condition="MemoryPressure",alertstate="firing"} or ALERTS{alertname="KubeNodePressure",node="$node",condition="MemoryPressure",alertstate="pending"})) or (0 * max(kube_node_status_condition{job="kube-state-metrics",node="$node",condition="MemoryPressure",status="true"}))) and on() ((max(up{job="kube-state-metrics"}) == 1) and on() (time() - max(timestamp(up{job="kube-state-metrics"})) < 90) and on() (time() - max(prometheus_rule_group_last_evaluation_timestamp_seconds{rule_group=~".*;socrat.nodes.health"}) < 90))

panels.title: Disk pressure
panels.description: DiskPressure reported by Kubernetes for 5 minutes, including pressure on free space or inodes. Color represents alert state at the end of the selected period: green is normal, amber is pending. No telemetry means Kubernetes state or rule-evaluation data is unavailable. Open the node to inspect it in Rancher.

targets.expr: ((max(2 * ALERTS{alertname="KubeNodePressure",node="$node",condition="DiskPressure",alertstate="firing"} or ALERTS{alertname="KubeNodePressure",node="$node",condition="DiskPressure",alertstate="pending"})) or (0 * max(kube_node_status_condition{job="kube-state-metrics",node="$node",condition="DiskPressure",status="true"}))) and on() ((max(up{job="kube-state-metrics"}) == 1) and on() (time() - max(timestamp(up{job="kube-state-metrics"})) < 90) and on() (time() - max(prometheus_rule_group_last_evaluation_timestamp_seconds{rule_group=~".*;socrat.nodes.health"}) < 90))

panels.title: PID pressure
panels.description: PIDPressure reported by Kubernetes for 5 minutes. Color represents alert state at the end of the selected period: green is normal, amber is pending. No telemetry means Kubernetes state or rule-evaluation data is unavailable. Open the node to inspect it in Rancher.

targets.expr: ((max(2 * ALERTS{alertname="KubeNodePressure",node="$node",condition="PIDPressure",alertstate="firing"} or ALERTS{alertname="KubeNodePressure",node="$node",condition="PIDPressure",alertstate="pending"})) or (0 * max(kube_node_status_condition{job="kube-state-metrics",node="$node",condition="PIDPressure",status="true"}))) and on() ((max(up{job="kube-state-metrics"}) == 1) and on() (time() - max(timestamp(up{job="kube-state-metrics"})) < 90) and on() (time() - max(prometheus_rule_group_last_evaluation_timestamp_seconds{rule_group=~".*;socrat.nodes.health"}) < 90))

panels.title: Scheduling
panels.description: Scheduling disabled (cordoned) for 15 minutes. This informational alert can indicate intentional maintenance; existing pods keep running. Color represents alert state at the end of the selected period: green is normal, amber is pending. No telemetry means Kubernetes state or rule-evaluation data is unavailable. Open the node to inspect it in Rancher.

targets.expr: ((max(2 * ALERTS{alertname="SocratNodeSchedulingDisabled",node="$node",alertstate="firing"} or ALERTS{alertname="SocratNodeSchedulingDisabled",node="$node",alertstate="pending"})) or (0 * max(kube_node_spec_unschedulable{job="kube-state-metrics",node="$node"}))) and on() ((max(up{job="kube-state-metrics"}) == 1) and on() (time() - max(timestamp(up{job="kube-state-metrics"})) < 90) and on() (time() - max(prometheus_rule_group_last_evaluation_timestamp_seconds{rule_group=~".*;socrat.nodes.health"}) < 90))

panels.title: Metrics freshness
panels.description: No successful node-exporter sample for more than 2 minutes, or no recorded sample within 24 hours; alert waits 1 additional minute before firing. This does not prove the node is down. Color represents alert state at the end of the selected period: green is normal, amber is pending. No telemetry means Kubernetes state or rule-evaluation data is unavailable. Open the node to inspect it in Rancher.

targets.expr: ((max(2 * ALERTS{alertname="SocratNodeMetricsStale",node="$node",alertstate="firing"} or ALERTS{alertname="SocratNodeMetricsStale",node="$node",alertstate="pending"})) or (0 * max(kube_node_info{job="kube-state-metrics",node="$node"}))) and on() ((max(up{job="kube-state-metrics"}) == 1) and on() (time() - max(timestamp(up{job="kube-state-metrics"})) < 90) and on() (time() - max(prometheus_rule_group_last_evaluation_timestamp_seconds{rule_group=~".*;socrat.nodes.health"}) < 90))

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since each selected node last booted, evaluated at the end of the selected time range. A drop indicates a reboot or a change in the reported boot time; this is host uptime, not container uptime.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((time() - node_boot_time_seconds{job="node-exporter"}) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Logical CPU cores
panels.description: Number of logical CPU cores exposed to the operating system on each selected node at the end of the selected time range. Includes hardware threads and virtual CPUs; this is capacity, not current utilization.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((count by(instance) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="node-exporter",mode="idle"})) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Physical memory
panels.description: Total RAM reported by the operating system on each selected node at the end of the selected time range. Displayed in byte-based units; this is total memory, not free memory or GPU memory.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{job="node-exporter"}) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Running pods
panels.description: Pods assigned to the selected node in the Running phase at the end of the selected period. Running does not guarantee that all containers are ready.

targets.expr: sum((max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Running"})) * on(namespace,pod) group_left(node) max by(namespace,pod,node) (kube_pod_info{node="$node"}))

panels.title: Unready pods
panels.description: Assigned, non-completed pods whose Ready condition is not true, including Pending pods. Evaluated at the end of the selected period; completed Jobs are excluded.

targets.expr: sum(((max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_ready{condition="true"}) == bool 0) and on(namespace,pod) (max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Running|Pending|Unknown"}) == 1)) * on(namespace,pod) group_left(node) max by(namespace,pod,node) (kube_pod_info{node="$node"}))

panels.title: Container restarts · selected period
panels.description: Estimated restarts over the selected period for containers in pods currently assigned to this node. Counter increases are extrapolated and may be fractional. Deleted pods and init containers are not included.

targets.expr: sum((sum by(namespace,pod) (max by(namespace,pod,container) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[$__range])))) * on(namespace,pod) group_left(node) max by(namespace,pod,node) (kube_pod_info{node="$node"}))

panels.title: Top pods · CPU cores
panels.description: Ten pods using the most CPU on the selected node at the end of the selected period. CPU seconds per second equal CPU cores; averaged over the automatic rate interval. Click a pod to open it in Rancher. Duplicate scrape series are removed before summing containers.

targets.expr: topk(10, (sum by(namespace,pod,node) (max by(namespace,pod,node,container) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{job="kubelet",metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor",node="$node",container!="",container!="POD"}[$__rate_interval])))) and on(namespace,pod) (max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Running|Pending|Unknown"}) == 1))

panels.title: Top pods · Memory
panels.description: Ten pods with the largest container memory working set on the selected node at the end of the selected period. Working set includes non-reclaimable cache and differs from process RSS. Click a pod to open it in Rancher.

targets.expr: topk(10, (sum by(namespace,pod,node) (max by(namespace,pod,node,container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{job="kubelet",metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor",node="$node",container!="",container!="POD"}))) and on(namespace,pod) (max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Running|Pending|Unknown"}) == 1))

panels.title: CPU · usage, requests and limits
panels.description: Container CPU usage in cores compared with declared requests, limits and node allocatable capacity. Requests and limits sum regular containers in active assigned pods; init-container maxima and pod overhead are excluded, so this is not the exact scheduler reservation. Requests reserve scheduling capacity, not physical usage. Containers without limits add no declared limit; the limits line is not an overall usage cap. Host processes are excluded from container usage.

targets.expr: sum((sum by(namespace,pod,node) (max by(namespace,pod,node,container) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{job="kubelet",metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor",node="$node",container!="",container!="POD"}[$__rate_interval])))) and on(namespace,pod) (max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Running|Pending|Unknown"}) == 1))

sum((max by(namespace,pod,container,node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{node="$node",resource="cpu"})) and on(namespace,pod) (max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Running|Pending|Unknown"}) == 1)) or (0 * max(kube_node_status_allocatable{node="$node",resource="cpu"}))

sum((max by(namespace,pod,container,node) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{node="$node",resource="cpu"})) and on(namespace,pod) (max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Running|Pending|Unknown"}) == 1)) or (0 * max(kube_node_status_allocatable{node="$node",resource="cpu"}))
max(kube_node_status_allocatable{node="$node",resource="cpu"})

panels.title: Memory · usage, requests and limits
panels.description: Container memory working set in bytes compared with declared requests, limits and node allocatable capacity. Requests and limits sum regular containers in active assigned pods; init-container maxima and pod overhead are excluded, so this is not the exact scheduler reservation. Requests reserve scheduling capacity, not physical usage. Containers without limits add no declared limit; the limits line is not an overall usage cap. Host processes are excluded from container usage.

targets.expr: sum((sum by(namespace,pod,node) (max by(namespace,pod,node,container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{job="kubelet",metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor",node="$node",container!="",container!="POD"}))) and on(namespace,pod) (max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Running|Pending|Unknown"}) == 1))

sum((max by(namespace,pod,container,node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{node="$node",resource="memory"})) and on(namespace,pod) (max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Running|Pending|Unknown"}) == 1)) or (0 * max(kube_node_status_allocatable{node="$node",resource="memory"}))

sum((max by(namespace,pod,container,node) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{node="$node",resource="memory"})) and on(namespace,pod) (max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Running|Pending|Unknown"}) == 1)) or (0 * max(kube_node_status_allocatable{node="$node",resource="memory"}))
max(kube_node_status_allocatable{node="$node",resource="memory"})

panels.title: CPU wait and steal
panels.description: Percentage of logical CPU time spent waiting for I/O or stolen by the hypervisor, averaged over the automatic rate interval. I/O wait can indicate storage contention; steal indicates a virtual machine waiting for host CPU. These are fractions of total CPU capacity, not task latency.

targets.expr: avg by(nodename) ((100 * avg by(instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="node-exporter",mode="iowait"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by(instance,nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

avg by(nodename) ((100 * avg by(instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="node-exporter",mode="steal"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by(instance,nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: CPU pressure
panels.description: Percentage of wall time during which at least one runnable task waited for CPU (Linux PSI some), averaged over the automatic rate interval. Measures contention, not CPU utilization. Unsupported or missing pressure metrics remain missing.

targets.expr: avg by(nodename) ((100 * rate(node_pressure_cpu_waiting_seconds_total{job="node-exporter"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by(instance,nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Memory pressure
panels.description: Linux PSI as a percentage of wall time over the automatic rate interval. Waiting means at least one task was stalled; fully stalled means all non-idle tasks were stalled on memory reclaim. Sustained pressure indicates lost execution time. Missing metrics are not replaced with zero.

targets.expr: avg by(nodename) ((100 * rate(node_pressure_memory_waiting_seconds_total{job="node-exporter"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by(instance,nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

avg by(nodename) ((100 * rate(node_pressure_memory_stalled_seconds_total{job="node-exporter"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by(instance,nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: I/O pressure
panels.description: Linux PSI as a percentage of wall time over the automatic rate interval. Waiting means at least one task was stalled; fully stalled means all non-idle tasks were stalled on I/O. Sustained pressure indicates lost execution time. Missing metrics are not replaced with zero.

targets.expr: avg by(nodename) ((100 * rate(node_pressure_io_waiting_seconds_total{job="node-exporter"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by(instance,nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

avg by(nodename) ((100 * rate(node_pressure_io_stalled_seconds_total{job="node-exporter"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by(instance,nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: CPU utilization
panels.description: Non-idle CPU time as a percentage of all logical CPU capacity, averaged over the automatic rate interval. Includes I/O wait. Near 100% means little idle CPU time remains; it does not distinguish computation from waiting for I/O.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((100 * (1 - avg by(instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="node-exporter",mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])))) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Load average per core
panels.description: Five-minute load average divided by the number of logical CPU cores. A value of 1 means an average of one runnable or uninterruptibly waiting task per core. Sustained values above 1 can indicate contention, but disk I/O waits also contribute; this is not CPU utilization.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((node_load5{job="node-exporter"} / on(instance) count by(instance) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="node-exporter",mode="idle"})) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Load average · 1 / 5 / 15 minutes
panels.description: Average number of runnable tasks and tasks in uninterruptible sleep, including disk I/O wait, over 1, 5 and 15 minutes. Compare with logical CPU core count to assess demand. These fixed averaging windows do not change with the dashboard time range.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((node_load1{job="node-exporter"}) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))
avg by (nodename) ((node_load5{job="node-exporter"}) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))
avg by (nodename) ((node_load15{job="node-exporter"}) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Memory utilization
panels.description: Percentage of RAM not available for new applications: total memory minus the kernel estimate of available memory. Reclaimable cache is accounted for. A rising percentage means less memory headroom.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((100 * (1 - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{job="node-exporter"} / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{job="node-exporter"})) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Available memory
panels.description: RAM the kernel estimates can be used by new applications without swapping, including reclaimable cache, in byte-based units. A falling value means less memory headroom.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{job="node-exporter"}) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Swap used
panels.description: Swap space currently used, in byte-based units. Zero may mean swap is unused or disabled. This measures stored pages, not the rate at which pages are being swapped.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((node_memory_SwapTotal_bytes{job="node-exporter"} - node_memory_SwapFree_bytes{job="node-exporter"}) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Root filesystem · used
panels.description: Percentage of the root filesystem unavailable to ordinary processes, including used space and filesystem reservations. Near 100% means little writable space remains; other mount points are not included.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((100 * (1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{job="node-exporter",mountpoint="/",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{job="node-exporter",mountpoint="/",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs"})) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Root filesystem · available
panels.description: Free root-filesystem space available to ordinary processes, in byte-based units. Filesystem reservations are excluded. A falling value means less room for application data, images and logs on this filesystem.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename) ((node_filesystem_avail_bytes{job="node-exporter",mountpoint="/",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs"}) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Disk I/O
panels.description: Read and write throughput per disk device, in bytes per second averaged over the automatic rate interval. Physical and logical devices are shown separately and should not be added together. Loop, RAM and optical devices are excluded.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename, device) ((rate(node_disk_read_bytes_total{job="node-exporter",device!~"loop.*|ram.*|sr.*"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

avg by (nodename, device) ((rate(node_disk_written_bytes_total{job="node-exporter",device!~"loop.*|ram.*|sr.*"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Inbound traffic
panels.description: Received traffic per network interface, in bytes per second averaged over the automatic rate interval. Includes WireGuard; container and loopback interfaces are excluded. Tunnel traffic may also cross a physical interface, so adding both can double-count it.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename, device) ((rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total{job="node-exporter",device!~"lo|veth.*|cali.*|cni.*|flannel.*|docker.*|br-.*"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Outbound traffic
panels.description: Transmitted traffic per network interface, in bytes per second averaged over the automatic rate interval. Includes WireGuard; container and loopback interfaces are excluded. Tunnel traffic may also cross a physical interface, so adding both can double-count it.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename, device) ((rate(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{job="node-exporter",device!~"lo|veth.*|cali.*|cni.*|flannel.*|docker.*|br-.*"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Network interface errors
panels.description: Receive and transmit errors per second on each network interface, averaged over the automatic rate interval. Nonzero values warrant checking that interface. This does not directly measure end-to-end packet loss or internet availability.

targets.expr: avg by (nodename, device) ((rate(node_network_receive_errs_total{job="node-exporter",device!~"lo|veth.*|cali.*|cni.*|flannel.*|docker.*|br-.*"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

avg by (nodename, device) ((rate(node_network_transmit_errs_total{job="node-exporter",device!~"lo|veth.*|cali.*|cni.*|flannel.*|docker.*|br-.*"}[$__rate_interval])) * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by (instance, nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))

panels.title: Maximum sensor temperature
panels.description: Highest reported hardware sensor temperature on each node, in degrees Celsius. Includes CPU and storage sensors, so the hottest device can change over time. The socrat-2 VPS exposes no sensors and has no series; missing data does not mean a temperature of zero.

targets.expr: max by(nodename) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius{job="node-exporter"} * on(instance) group_left(nodename) max by(instance,nodename) (node_uname_info{job="node-exporter",nodename="$node"}))
